newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Anti-APEC forum launches counter meeting.
newsitem.headline: Anti-APEC forum launches counter meeting.

text.p: An anti-APEC forum launched its meeting on Thursday night with a blast against free trade among Pacific Rim nations and a keynote address by an East Timorese dissident exile.

The chairman of the International Convenors Committee for the Manila People's Forum on APEC (MPFA), Walden Bello, said the MPFA comprised non-governmental organisations, people's groups and individuals opposed to the principles of APEC.
APEC, the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum, is holding its annual meeting in Manila to agree on strategies designed to produce free trade among its 18 members by the year 2020.

Bello, a sociology teacher at the University of the Philippines, said the MPFA was "united against the direction of becoming a free trade area marked by indiscriminate liberalisation of trade and investment".

Free trade, he said, primarily served the interest of the United States, which aimed at eliminating its trade deficit with Asia nations at the expense of the peoples of Asia following a policy of "economic realpolitik".
He said the counter forum was for equitable and sustainable development with a flexible trade policy.
"An enlightened government activism that demands a great deal of regulation of market forces is essential," he added.

The keynote speaker at the forum opening before several hundred people in a hotel ballroom was to have been Jose Ramos Horta, the self-exiled leader of the East Timorese resistance against Indonesian rule who was jointly awarded the Nobel Peace Prize last month.

The Philippines government banned him during the APEC conference and summit -- a move that has been challenged in the Supreme Court. He was replaced by another Australian-based East Timorese activist, Maria Bernardino.

Bernardino bitterly assailed Jakarta's rule in East Timor, the former Portuguese colony Indonesian troops invaded in December 1975 and which was incorporated as Indonesia's 27th province the following July in a move the United Nations refuses to recognise.
A message was read out from Ramos Horta, who is currently in Brazil.

"Your vigorous and concerned discussion will look at basic issues in our region which need to be urgently addressed before any economic model can be successful in reaching what should be its fundamental goals, the advancement of human well-being, peace and justice," he said.
The Philippines government hurriedly moved two APEC delegations -- from Papua New Guinea and Hong Kong -- out of the hotel when it was discovered the anti-forum was being held there.
